newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end lower as soybeans slide.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end lower as soybeans slide.

text.p: A late break to the day's lows in soybean futures knocked CBOT soy product futures to lower closes, traders said.
Soymeal traded lower throughout the session on profit taking but soyoil held firm until late in the day.
Soyoil was underpinned by signals of consumptive interest now that the market has dipped to near the 25.00 cent per lb level, traders said.
"Because of the price differential (U.S. versus others) we are now starting to see some European interest in oil," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.

There was talk in cash vegetable oil markets that some overseas customers might shun U.S. soyoil in favor of Canadian canola oil. But traders said the U.S. price now has dropped to a competitive level.
Traders also said there was talk Iraq, Morocco and Egypt were slated in the market next week for soyoil.
Soymeal was underpinned by tight cash supplies, firm cash basis markets and by commercial buying, they said.
Soyoil futures closed 0.08 to 0.20 cent per lb lower, with October down 0.11 at 24.45 cents. Soymeal finished $0.90 to $2.50 per ton lower, with October down $2.10 at $262.40.
Cargill Inc sold 450 December soyoil and ADM Investor Services bought 350 lots of October, they said.
Merrill Lynch Futures sold 250 December soymeal and Continental Grain bought 300 October and Refco Inc bought 350 December soymeal, traders said.
Soyoil futures volume was estimated at 16,000, down from 33,489 Thursday, according to the CBOT. Soymeal futures volume was estimated at 17,000, down from 29,470 Thursday.
